keyFindings.description: backfillBlockIDs reads the room's queue in flushThrough before it holds the document's advisory lock. A worker flush that has committed class A but not yet marked it stored passes the gate, so the backfill stores A a second time. The only guard is the assumption that the backfill's service serves no browser, and the PR's own TestStoredOrderBackfillStampOverAnUnstoredEdit breaks that assumption. Fix: lockDocumentRoom right after Begin; move the stale-room test's window to a hook before Begin; delete the exception text in service.go and flush.go.

The backfill builds a Ledger with settling: true, but ledger.go:25-34 says settlement's and the joined ledger are the only two. Update the doc, or rename the field to what it means (a transaction of its own).
takeRoomCursors decides twice, with opposite tests, whether a write and a flush share an instance (:240 and :248). Decide it once.

appendingCursor's comment says a joined transaction's flush is read by the room-cursor branch; flushThrough passes flush to every flush append, so the flush branch decides those, and the ledger lookup serves only the repairs storeRepair appends.
